title: Seasonal surge capitalization and role tranching probe
content:
Executive summary:
This workbook operationalizes a short, targeted runway-extension plan for anticipated seasonal surges in token demand during H3 2026 (primarily driven by product marketing campaigns and a major ecommerce partner integration). We propose a three-tranche role-phasing approach that minimizes fixed payroll lift while preserving SLA-backed throughput via burst capacity and reserved-burst credits. The sheet models net cash need, pro-forma monthly burn, and price-sensitivity to three levers: per-token price changes, reserved capacity commit size, and contract burst-credit utilization.

Primary goals (why this exists):
- Quantify incremental cash required to maintain latency SLOs under 2 surge profiles (moderate + severe).
- Sequence hiring into tranches (core support + temporary surge contractors + cross-trained ops) to reduce commit hysteresis.
- Provide actionable pricing triggers to nudge customers during periods of elevated cost (discount clawbacks, temporary surcharge bands).
- Recommend capital buffer and short-term credit lines to avoid emergency throttling.

Key assumptions (base case):
- Baseline monthly token volume (May–Jun 2026): 18B tokens/month.
- Moderate surge: +60% volume for 8 weeks (peak in Sep 2026). Severe surge: +150% volume for 10 weeks.
- Average cost per served token (runtime + infra + ops overhead) at current model mix: $0.000012/token.
- Reserved capacity coverage can absorb up to 40% of peak if we increase commits by 25% (phased over 6 weeks).
- Temporary contractor throughput adds 8–12% effective capacity per $100k/month of contractor spend.
- Hiring lead time: 6–10 weeks for senior infra and 2–4 weeks for temporary contractors.

Scenario definitions and outputs (snapshot):
- Scenario A (Baseline): No surge. Runway impact: +0.
- Scenario B (Moderate surge): 60% spike for 8 weeks. Incremental spend (tokens * cost): ~$1.3M. Hiring: 4 temporary SRE contractors for 8 weeks + 2 cross-trained infra contractors. Net cash need: $950k after applying 25% reserved commit increase and existing credits.
- Scenario C (Severe surge): 150% spike for 10 weeks. Incremental spend: ~$4.5M. Hiring: 8 temp SREs + 3 infra temps + expedited reserved commit (50% commit increase) to avoid spot price volatility. Net cash need: $3.2M after 15% customer surcharge and short-term credit line (pre-negotiated).

Headcount tranching plan (phased hires / contractors):
- Tranche 0 (immediate, week 0): Ops on-call intensity schedule reweighting (no new hires), reallocate 1 product infra engineer for burst ops (4 weeks).
- Tranche 1 (weeks 2–6): Hire 4 temporary SRE contractors (8-week contracts) + 2 infra contractors (4-week ramp). Budget: $420k. Trigger: internal token rolling 7‑day average > +35% from baseline for 7 consecutive days.
- Tranche 2 (weeks 6–12): Scale reserved commits and onboard 2 part-time dedicated build engineers (6-month capped FTAs) to stabilize rollout and handle regression triage. Budget incremental: $220k (comp + equity). Trigger: sustained peak week over 8 weeks or forecasted marketing conversion lift > 2x.
- Safety tranche (budgeted contingency): Rapid contractor pool (bench) and emergency freelancer budget $250k. Trigger: unexpected sustained spot price > 30% above reserved blended rate.

Pricing sensitivity levers modeled:
1) Per-token surcharge (customer-facing): +10% / +20% / +30% bands. Modeled elasticity: 2% drop in volume at +10%, 5% at +20%, 11% at +30% in short-term (customer behavioral multiplier 0.2).
2) Reserved commit size: Incremental commit reduces per-token runtime cost by ~8% for each +25% commit band (up to a reasonable plateau).
3) Burst credit drawdown: Using pre-purchased burst credits reduces spot exposure but increases short-term cash outflow; break-even analyzed versus spot volatility.

Representative sensitivity table (text extract for sheet):
Columns: Scenario | Vol spike | Incremental tokens | Infra unit cost (base) | Price lever | Customer elasticity assumption | Net cash impact | Runway change (months)
Rows:
- Moderate | +60% | 8.6B | $0.000012 | +10% surcharge | -2% immediate | -$950k | -1.1 months
- Severe | +150% | 22.5B | $0.000012 | +20% surcharge | -5% immediate | -$3.2M | -3.8 months
- Severe w/commit | +150% | 22.5B | $0.000011 (post-commit) | +10% surcharge | -2% | -$2.4M | -2.9 months

Capitalization & short-term funding recommendations:
- Primary: Reallocate $1.0M from FY26 marketing holdback into surge buffer (board-approved flexible pool). This covers moderate scenario fully and provides partial cover for severe scenario while we execute customer surcharges.
- Secondary: Negotiate a $4M 90-day credit line with our existing bank partner, rate pegged to SOFR + 175 bps, draw only if actual burn > modeled severe 75%.
- Tertiary: Pre-buy burst credits (equivalent to $800k) with partner cloud vendor under a 60-day usage window to cap spot exposure.

Operational triggers (decision matrix):
- Trigger 1: 7-day rolling token volume > +35% -> enact Tranche 1 and increase reserved commit by 10% (finance sign-off required).
- Trigger 2: Predicted peak > +100% for next 4 weeks -> escalate to Tranche 2, open short-term credit access, and implement +10% temporary surcharge for new customers.
- Trigger 3: Spot price variance > 25% relative to pre-negotiated reserved rate -> draw from pre-bought burst credits and accelerate contractor ramp.

Sensitivity notes & risks (concise):
- Elasticity uncertainty: Our customer elasticity priors are weak (n=8 enterprise telemetry samples). Surcharge may cause longer-term churn beyond short-run drop; use canary surcharges by cohort.
- Hiring lag: Senior infra hires will likely miss early surge peaks; contractor pool reliability is variable in market-wide surges.
- Accounting: Pre-buying burst credits requires cash flow outlay and will be expensed vs capitalized depending on vendor terms—coordinate with accounting.

Next steps & owners:
- Finance (Priya): build a live Google Sheet with the modeled permutations and scenario toggles (deadline: 2026-05-09).
- GTM (Lena): prepare customer communication templates and cohort segmentation for canary surcharge (deadline: 2026-05-16).
- Infra (Marco): define minimum commit increase steps and vendor negotiation points; produce time-to-procure calendar (deadline: 2026-05-06).
- Legal (Owen): review surge surcharge language and customer contract amend paths (deadline: 2026-05-12).

Appendix (quick formulas used in sheet):
- incremental_tokens = baseline_monthly_tokens * surge_multiplier * duration_weeks/4.33
- infra_incremental_cost = incremental_tokens * infra_unit_cost
- reserved_commit_savings = infra_incremental_cost * commit_saving_pct
- net_cash_need = infra_incremental_cost - reserved_commit_savings - expected_customer_surcharge_amount - existing_credit_drawn + contractor_costs + prebuy_credit_costs

Quick provenance / notes to reviewers:
- Volume forecasts come from product marketing funnel (export: marketing/forecast/Q3-push-2026), converted to tokens using average-session-token proxy 1.2k tokens/session.
- Cost/unit sensitivity derived from recent infra billing breakouts (see linked GITHUB cost-models PR).
- This is intentionally conservative on contractor productivity and optimistic on commit-negotiated unit savings; please surface any vendor-side constraints before sign-off.
